newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast power mostly steady in light trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast power mostly steady in light trade.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the U.S. Southeast were mostly steady Monday in light activity as traders prepared for the upcoming holiday amid mild weather in the region.
"Everything's is pretty much status quo today. There aren't a lot of traders out there," one market source said.

Firm, peak power prices in the northern part of the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) territory for Tuesday were assessed in the $11.00-$12.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range, as compared with Friday's wider range of $11.00-13.00.
Firm, off-peak electricity in northern TVA was still notionally assessed in the $8.50-9.00 range.

At the Georgia/Florida border, prices for firm, peak electricity in 16 hour blocks for Tuesday delivery were fairly steady in the $18.50-20.00 range, as compared with Friday's $19.00-20.00 trading range.
Firm, off-peak power for Tuesday at the Ga./Fla. border was steady at $9.00.
In Florida, firm, peak power prices on a 16-hour schedule were mostly steady in the $21.00-22.00 area as overcast skies and above-normal temperatures kept demand at a minimum.
Temperatures in the Southeast are expected to remain at least 10-18 degrees above-normal over the next couple of days amid sporadic thunderstorms.
